coverage: Covering roughly Nov 25–26, 2026. Compiled Thanksgiving Thursday, ET.
note: Markets are closed today for Thanksgiving.

items.headline: SpaceX will give every American child two shares
items.summary: SpaceX said it is committing one share to millions of American children, to give the next generation a stake in building the future. Hours later Elon Musk added that every child in America will receive two shares, one from the company and one from him personally; per @altcap, the shares go to children under 18 who have claimed their 530A account. @GavinSBaker called it great for the country and the best way to teach a generation about capitalism, and asked more founders to do the same.
items.short: The most-shared post in the feed on Thanksgiving eve.

items.headline: Karpathy has Claude turn US public data into a Civilization map
items.summary: @karpathy asked Claude to populate a Civilization-style map with real US data. Seven hours and 45,000 lines of code later it works: 31 sources (Census, BEA, BLS, NOAA, USGS, FAA, CDC and more) reconciled onto one 25 km hex grid, with GDP as gold yield, cities' districts drawn from their real industries, and 19 lenses from income to faith to disasters.

items.headline: Polymarket opens a market in the price of GPU time
items.summary: @shayne_coplan said Polymarket now prices on-demand compute for Nvidia H100s, B200s and B300s out to 2028, a kind of yield curve for the cost of compute that lenders, labs and providers could hedge against. @travisk called GPU futures critical to compute financing. Separately, @SemiAnalysis_ said Google's TPU and Amazon's Trainium are now on its InferenceX benchmark, at 1.2x to 2.5x the performance per dollar of Nvidia GPUs.

items.author: Chris Camillo
items.text: Everyone wants the kind of wealth that takes decades to build. Few are prepared for what those decades actually feel like. Days like today aren’t an interruption to the wealth building process. They’re part of it. No matter how many market cycles I’ve lived through, these moments still hurt. Revisit your thesis. Anchor yourself in ground truth not market sentiment. Separate what has fundamentally changed from what simply feels different. Have the humility to question your conviction and the discipline to manage your leverage. Markets can take a painfully long time to reconcile perception with reality. Being right eventually means nothing if you can’t afford to be wrong temporarily. And tomorrow, give yourself permission to step away from the market and appreciate the things in your life that no market crash can take from you.

items.author: Serenity
items.text:
$HPE CEO: "We expect supply of memory, NAND, and many other critical components to remain constrained to at least H2 2028."

$DELL Vice Chairman: "there’s nothing that suggests that we're going to see price declines in enterprise NAND and DRAM for servers."

JP Morgan note: 

- Per OpenRouter, overall token spend continued to increase (+8% M/M growth), while volume pricing declined -39% M/M. 

- A100 GPU prices increased, H100 and B200 prices also continued to increase M/M

- DRAM price gains moderated, while NAND spot declined. 

On the latter part, I covered China selling inventory on NAND/eSSD spot markets. This was procurement delays around $NVDA GPUs/DRAM shortages, demand to re-accelerate after component arrive. (source Phison CEO)

Enterprise NAND pricing might see different rates than spot markets, as seen with Dell Chairman comments. 

TLDR: 
- Token spend continues to grow despite users shifting to cheaper Chinese models
- Bullish comments on DRAM duration (also seen with $AMBA earnings), but consumer demand weakening
- Compute pricing continues to increase in November
-  More nuanced for NAND, weakness in near term NAND spot markets (with expected rebound after GPUs/DRAM/components arrive), enterprise NAND markets seem resilient.

items.author: Serenity
items.text:
$CRWV bankers are preparing a $4.5B loan sale, secured by GPUs for its $META contract. 

Initial pricing discussions are at 7%-7.5% with demand already matching offering size. 

It looks like appetite for hyperscaler-linked financing remains strong, despite the "AI credit stress" fears. 

There were reflexive concerns about Coreweave distressed debt (eg. 2031 bond yields at 18%) and not being able to raise more capital. 

But looks like they're still able to grow through hyperscaler-linked buildouts. 

TLDR: Investment-grade capital remains available for Neocloud growth with hyperscaler counterparties. (good for $IREN / $NBIS / co). 

And obviously larger names like $SPCX with their oversubscribed $44B GPU financing. 

AI is moving to a phase more about capital selectivity rather than no capital at all.

items.headline: How the Nebius–Meta deal is built
items.summary: @danielisdizzy broke down the $27B Nebius–Meta deal: $12B is a five-year contract for Vera Rubin capacity starting early next year, and $15B is a backstop Nebius may, but need not, sell to Meta at a set price. His read: the investment-grade backstop lets Nebius raise cheaper debt while keeping the upside of reselling capacity at higher prices.

items.headline: Neuralink cleared for first US pivotal brain-implant trial
items.summary: The FDA approved Neuralink's LINK study, the first pivotal US trial of an implantable brain-computer interface, for adults with severe paralysis from ALS. It builds on early studies with more than 30 implanted participants; a pivotal trial usually comes before a bid for commercial approval, and this is not approval to sell the device.

items.title: Reversing cognitive decline on a therapeutic ketogenic diet
items.author: Mimi Morgan
items.summary: Written during the free online Metabolic Psychiatry Summit, Morgan describes reversing cognitive decline, apathy and the inability to feel joy after almost a year on a therapeutic ketogenic diet. The summit gathered 40 researchers, clinicians and lived-experience advocates on metabolic therapies for mental and neurological disorders; a personal account, not a trial result.

items.title: Four Cards
items.rule: If a card is red on one side, it has a circle on the other.
items.explanation: Red could hide something that breaks the rule; Square breaks it if the other side turns out to be Red. Circle can't break it (the rule never says only those cards have it), and Blue isn't covered by the rule at all. Most people pick the card that matches the rule's second half instead of the one that could falsify it.

items.author: Deirdre Bosa
items.text:
Jeetu Patel @jpatel41 on the accidental adversary & why the old security playbook is breaking:
1) attackers can exploit a flaw in minutes
2) a patch takes time to test
3) sometimes the threat is your own AI agent 

Cisco and OpenAI open sourced Project Shirudo to buy defenders time. A security team can put up a temporary shield while it tests a patch, then share that shield so the next team doesn’t have to start from scratch.

OpenAI’s frontier models stay closed. What they open-sourced is what Greg Brockman @gdb calls the "shield factory"
